subject: math
cluster: Define trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right triangles
skillName: Sine and Cosine of Complementary Angles
description: Students explain and use the co-function relationship for acute angles in a right triangle: the sine of an angle equals the cosine of its complement, and the cosine of an angle equals the sine of its complement. Concretely, if $A$ and $B$ are the two acute angles of a right triangle then $A + B = 90^\circ$, and $\sin A = \cos B = \cos(90^\circ - A)$ while $\cos A = \sin B = \sin(90^\circ - A)$. Students justify this from the side-ratio definitions (the leg opposite one acute angle is the leg adjacent to the other), rewrite expressions between sine and cosine, evaluate co-function statements, and solve equations such as $\sin(2x) = \cos(x + 30^\circ)$ by setting the angles complementary.
subSkills: State and explain why $\sin\theta = \cos(90^\circ - \theta)$ and $\cos\theta = \sin(90^\circ - \theta)$ for acute $\theta$ using the opposite/adjacent leg-swap in a right triangle
Given $\sin A$ for one acute angle, state $\cos B$ for the complementary angle (and vice versa) without recomputing ratios
Rewrite a sine as a cosine of the complement (or a cosine as a sine of the complement)
Evaluate whether a co-function equation is true and find a missing angle that makes two trig values equal
Solve $\sin(\text{expr}_1) = \cos(\text{expr}_2)$ by setting $\text{expr}_1 + \text{expr}_2 = 90^\circ$ and solving the resulting linear equation
Apply the relationship in right-triangle contexts and with the radian co-function form $\sin\theta = \cos\!\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - \theta\right)$

problemArchetypes.name: State the complement value
problemArchetypes.example: In right triangle $ABC$ with $\angle C = 90^\circ$, $\sin A = \frac{5}{13}$. What is $\cos B$? Answer: $\frac{5}{13}$.

problemArchetypes.name: Rewrite sine as cosine of complement
problemArchetypes.example: Rewrite $\sin 37^\circ$ as the cosine of an angle. Answer: $\cos 53^\circ$.

problemArchetypes.name: Find the missing angle that equates sine and cosine
problemArchetypes.example: Find the acute angle $\theta$ so that $\sin 28^\circ = \cos\theta$. Answer: $\theta = 62^\circ$.

problemArchetypes.name: Radian / exact-value co-function
problemArchetypes.example: Express $\cos\frac{\pi}{5}$ as a sine. Answer: $\sin\frac{3\pi}{10}$, since $\frac{\pi}{2} - \frac{\pi}{5} = \frac{3\pi}{10}$.

problemArchetypes.name: Explain / justify the relationship
problemArchetypes.example: Using right triangle $ABC$ with $\angle C = 90^\circ$, explain why $\sin A = \cos B$. The leg opposite $A$ is the leg adjacent to $B$, and both ratios use the same hypotenuse, so $\frac{\text{opp } A}{\text{hyp}} = \frac{\text{adj } B}{\text{hyp}}$.

Easy.description: Direct one-step recall of the co-function relationship with integer degree measures or a single given ratio. Student either reads off $\cos B$ from a given $\sin A$, rewrites $\sin\theta$ as $\cos(90^\circ - \theta)$ for a numeric $\theta$, or checks a true/false statement. No equation solving.
constraints: Angles are whole-number degrees with an obvious complement (e.g. $30^\circ$, $40^\circ$, $65^\circ$)
Given values are simple fractions or single named angles; no $x$ to solve for

Medium.description: Two-step problems: find the acute angle that makes $\sin a = \cos b$, or solve a single-variable linear co-function equation where each side is a simple expression in $x$. Includes mixing a given right-triangle ratio with the complement and one radian-form rewrite. Requires setting up $a + b = 90^\circ$ (or $\frac{\pi}{2}$) and solving once.
constraints: Solve one linear equation of the form $\sin(\alpha x + c) = \cos(\beta x + d)$ with small integer coefficients
May use radians with $\frac{\pi}{2}$ as the complement total
Single complement set-up; answer is an exact angle (degrees or a $\pi$ fraction)

Hard.description: Multi-step or justification-heavy: solve a co-function equation requiring distribution/combining like terms, then a follow-up (e.g. evaluate a triangle angle or verify); explain WHY the relationship holds from the leg-swap definition; or chain the identity with a Pythagorean/right-triangle computation to produce an exact value. May require recognizing that two distinct trig expressions are equal only when their angles are complementary and checking the acute-angle domain.
constraints: Equation set-up needs distribution and simplification before isolating $x$, or yields a follow-up quantity
Includes at least one justification or explanation of the co-function identity from triangle definitions
May combine co-function rewriting with exact values ($\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, $\frac{1}{2}$) or radian measures

difficultyRubric.tierSplit: If split into two worksheets: tier1 covers Easy to Medium (state-the-complement, rewrite sine/cosine, true/false checks, find-the-missing-angle, and single-step linear co-function equations). tier2 covers Medium to Hard (multi-term linear co-function equations with distribution, radian-form problems, justification/explanation items, and identity-plus-exact-value chains). No item overlap between tiers.

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Thinks sine and cosine of the SAME angle are equal, ignoring the complement
commonMisconceptions.distractor: For $\sin A = \frac{5}{13}$ answers $\cos A = \frac{5}{13}$ (claims $\cos B$ uses the same angle) instead of recognizing $\cos B = \sin A$ because $B$ is the complement

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Sets the two angles EQUAL instead of complementary when solving $\sin a = \cos b$
commonMisconceptions.distractor: Solves $2x = x + 30^\circ$ to get $x = 30^\circ$ instead of $2x + (x+30^\circ) = 90^\circ$ giving $x = 20^\circ$
Computes the complement as $180^\circ - \theta$, e.g. rewrites $\sin 37^\circ$ as $\cos 143^\circ$ instead of $\cos 53^\circ$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Forgets the co-function swaps sine and cosine; keeps the same function name
Subtracts from $90^\circ$ incorrectly or arithmetic slip on the complement
commonMisconceptions.distractor: Gives the complement of $28^\circ$ as $72^\circ$ instead of $62^\circ$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Uses $\frac{\pi}{2}$ wrong in radians (e.g. complements with $\pi$)

_comment_itemCounts: Single ramped worksheet (Easy->Hard across 15 items) suffices for most standards; tier1/tier2 fields provided per schema for the complex-standard option.
